nodes.name: Lantern Rain
nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.dialogue: The rain makes every case glow, like the cartridges are dreaming under glass.{pause}I promised myself one final purchase, which is how every dangerous evening begins.{pause}Star Ferry Chronicle is the last blue spine missing from my little shelf.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}The four-note market tune loops once, brighter on the last note than the first.{pause}Tonight the hunt is less about owning a thing than learning why it survived.

nodes.name: Price Tag Weather
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: That price tag has crossed out three numbers and developed a personality.{pause}The vendor calls it rare, but he also called instant noodles vintage provisions.{pause}Let us inspect the story before we start negotiating with the sticker.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}Neither collector hurries; careful hands are part of the pleasure tonight.{pause}Every answer creates a smaller question, which is how good collecting works.

nodes.name: The Shared List
nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.dialogue: Our list began on a receipt when neither of us owned a working WonderSwan.{pause}You found the console, I found the battery door, and rain found everything else.{pause}Completing it should feel triumphant, yet I mostly feel afraid of finishing.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}Somewhere nearby, a vendor laughs and snaps another plastic case shut.{pause}They leave room for doubt instead of filling it with a convenient rumor.

nodes.name: A Blue Shell
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: No label, blue shell, gold contacts, and one tiny crescent scratched by the screw.{pause}This is either treasure, trouble, or a sports game wearing excellent camouflage.{pause}Whatever it is, somebody kept it close enough to polish the corners smooth.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}The little screen catches Mina's face, then Ren's, then only blue light.{pause}The bazaar keeps moving, but this one small mystery holds them still.

nodes.name: Vendor's Rule
nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.dialogue: The vendor says we may test it only if we buy tea from his sister.{pause}That is not a rule; that is a family business plan with excellent timing.{pause}I buy two cups, because mysteries are easier when your hands are warm.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}A tram bell crosses the rain and makes the whole stall feel briefly afloat.{pause}A rare cart can be expensive; a good story asks for a different kind of care.

nodes.name: Quiet Inventory
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: Case first: no cracks, no swelling, and no smell of a drowned attic.{pause}Contacts next, then shell screws, then whatever history the seller remembers.{pause}Collectors call this ritual, but really it is respect wearing a checklist.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}Their shared list softens at the folds from years of being opened together.{pause}Mina writes one clean line in the ledger before either of them moves on.

nodes.name: Koto in Pencil
nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.dialogue: There is a name inside the sleeve, written lightly in pencil: Koto.{pause}Not a shop code; the letters lean like someone writing on a moving train.{pause}The name turns the cart from an object into a message we have not earned yet.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}Even the silence feels playable, like a title screen waiting for one button.{pause}Ren checks the time, smiles, and decides the last tram can wait a little.

nodes.name: Forum Smoke
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: Moonlit Swan Almanac appeared on old forums, always without a clear photograph.{pause}Half the posts called it canceled, and the other half claimed one secret printing.{pause}Rumors survive because every collector leaves one empty space for impossible things.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}Ren taps the case twice, their old signal for a find worth remembering.{pause}The tune returns to its opening phrase, now sounding almost like a promise.

nodes.name: Blue Receipt
nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.dialogue: The biscuit tin receipt lists three puzzle carts and one item called blue book.{pause}The date is fourteen years old, but the ink still matches the sleeve note.{pause}If blue book means this cart, Koto bought it on the last market night.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}The four-note market tune loops once, brighter on the last note than the first.{pause}Tonight the hunt is less about owning a thing than learning why it survived.

nodes.name: Tea Steam
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: Before we chase ghosts, drink your tea; you always forget during a good find.{pause}You did the same when we found the pearl console and nearly fainted beside it.{pause}A collection should lengthen your life, not turn every flea market into a duel.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}Neither collector hurries; careful hands are part of the pleasure tonight.{pause}Every answer creates a smaller question, which is how good collecting works.

nodes.name: Almost Complete
nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.dialogue: I thought the finished shelf would prove those broke student years led somewhere.{pause}But the best part was never the row; it was calling you after each ridiculous lead.{pause}Maybe completion is frightening because the calls might stop when the gaps do.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}Somewhere nearby, a vendor laughs and snaps another plastic case shut.{pause}They leave room for doubt instead of filling it with a convenient rumor.

nodes.name: Ren's Duplicate
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: Then take my secret: I already own two copies of Harbor Cooking Club.{pause}I kept the second because finding it with you was funnier than selling it.{pause}The list is an excuse, Mina; friendship is allowed to be badly cataloged.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}The little screen catches Mina's face, then Ren's, then only blue light.{pause}The bazaar keeps moving, but this one small mystery holds them still.

nodes.name: Vendor Memory
nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.dialogue: He remembers Koto trading here with a yellow umbrella and a strict spending limit.{pause}She tested every cart twice, then gave the cheaper one to a waiting child.{pause}That sounds less like a legendary collector and more like someone we would like.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}A tram bell crosses the rain and makes the whole stall feel briefly afloat.{pause}A rare cart can be expensive; a good story asks for a different kind of care.

nodes.name: The Test Swan
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: The stall console has one bright pixel, two tired buttons, and heroic batteries.{pause}If the cart boots here, we owe this old machine a place in the credits.{pause}If it does not, we still have a name, a receipt, and a better evening.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}Their shared list softens at the folds from years of being opened together.{pause}Mina writes one clean line in the ledger before either of them moves on.

nodes.name: First Contact
nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.dialogue: The screen flashes blue, then draws a moon over a tiny black harbor.{pause}No logo appears; only a chime and the words, please return by dawn.{pause}My hands are shaking, so you are officially responsible for pressing Start.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}Even the silence feels playable, like a title screen waiting for one button.{pause}Ren checks the time, smiles, and decides the last tram can wait a little.

nodes.name: A Living Rumor
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: It is real, but not the way the forums imagined a commercial release.{pause}This looks handmade: simple maps, personal dates, and Koto's name in the menu.{pause}We may be holding a diary that happens to understand directional buttons.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}Ren taps the case twice, their old signal for a find worth remembering.{pause}The tune returns to its opening phrase, now sounding almost like a promise.

nodes.name: How to Begin
nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.dialogue: Before we go deeper, we choose what kind of guests we are in Koto's cart.{pause}We can study the hardware, ask for the seller's full memory, or follow the paper trail.{pause}The first method will decide which details we notice when dawn arrives.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}The four-note market tune loops once, brighter on the last note than the first.{pause}Tonight the hunt is less about owning a thing than learning why it survived.

nodes.name: Careful Current
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: Under the stall lamp, the contacts show three deliberate bridges made by hand.{pause}They are not repairs; they let the cart read the console clock through a spare pin.{pause}Our hardware check explains the station trick and proves Koto built this herself.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}Neither collector hurries; careful hands are part of the pleasure tonight.{pause}Every answer creates a smaller question, which is how good collecting works.

nodes.name: Yellow Umbrella
nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.dialogue: The vendor remembers Koto waiting after closing to give away duplicate puzzle carts.{pause}She called the blue one a lighthouse and asked him to pass it to two friends.{pause}His memory makes us part of a planned handoff, not lucky buyers at a stall.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}Somewhere nearby, a vendor laughs and snaps another plastic case shut.{pause}They leave room for doubt instead of filling it with a convenient rumor.

nodes.name: Folded Map
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: Behind the tray, a folded tram map carries tiny moons at seven stations.{pause}The pencil pressure matches Koto's name, and the final moon circles the bazaar roof.{pause}The paper route gives us a path and warns that the last choice cannot be undone.{pause}Rain freckles the glass while a hundred tiny prices shine like harbor lights.{pause}The little screen catches Mina's face, then Ren's, then only blue light.{pause}The bazaar keeps moving, but this one small mystery holds them still.

nodes.name: Last Tram
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: We carry the test console onto the last tram with the vendor's permission.{pause}Koto's little harbor advances only when the real tram passes certain stations.{pause}A handmade game tied to a timetable is exactly the kind of trouble I respect.{pause}The late tram rocks gently, and every loose case clicks in patient rhythm.{pause}A tram bell crosses the rain and makes the whole stall feel briefly afloat.{pause}A rare cart can be expensive; a good story asks for a different kind of care.

nodes.name: Ninety-Nine Hours
nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.dialogue: One save file reads KOTO, ninety-nine hours, with the final stamp still empty.{pause}Nobody accidentally plays a tiny map for ninety-nine hours; this was a ritual.{pause}The unfinished stamp feels less like failure and more like a door held open.{pause}The late tram rocks gently, and every loose case clicks in patient rhythm.{pause}Their shared list softens at the folds from years of being opened together.{pause}Mina writes one clean line in the ledger before either of them moves on.

nodes.name: Station Messages
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: Each stop reveals one sentence: buy what you love, lend what you can.{pause}At our station it adds, leave one mystery for the next pair of hands.{pause}Koto did not hide a rare game; she built instructions for future collectors.{pause}The late tram rocks gently, and every loose case clicks in patient rhythm.{pause}Even the silence feels playable, like a title screen waiting for one button.{pause}Ren checks the time, smiles, and decides the last tram can wait a little.

nodes.name: The Missing Stamp
nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.dialogue: The final stamp asks for a decision, not a password or a perfect score.{pause}Preserve Koto's route, begin our own, or copy the map and leave both untouched.{pause}Any button will change the object, even if the change is only in us.{pause}The late tram rocks gently, and every loose case clicks in patient rhythm.{pause}Ren taps the case twice, their old signal for a find worth remembering.{pause}The tune returns to its opening phrase, now sounding almost like a promise.

nodes.name: Rooftop Invitation
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: The last message names the bazaar roof and says to arrive before the rain clears.{pause}Our stop is behind us, the batteries are low, and I am absolutely going.{pause}You can blame the cart, but we both know we were already climbing.{pause}The late tram rocks gently, and every loose case clicks in patient rhythm.{pause}The four-note market tune loops once, brighter on the last note than the first.{pause}Tonight the hunt is less about owning a thing than learning why it survived.

nodes.name: The Unpressed Button
nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.dialogue: I move the cursor to New Route, then back away without confirming.{pause}Koto's ninety-nine hours remain exactly where she left them, final stamp waiting.{pause}Preserving it feels active now, not timid, because we understand what stays open.{pause}Above the bazaar, wet roofs hold the city upside down in their puddles.{pause}Neither collector hurries; careful hands are part of the pleasure tonight.{pause}Every answer creates a smaller question, which is how good collecting works.

nodes.name: Two New Names
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: We photograph Koto's screen, then choose New Route and enter MINA plus REN.{pause}The first harbor light turns on beside the old save instead of replacing it.{pause}The cart has room for inheritance and change, which is kinder than we expected.{pause}Above the bazaar, wet roofs hold the city upside down in their puddles.{pause}Somewhere nearby, a vendor laughs and snaps another plastic case shut.{pause}They leave room for doubt instead of filling it with a convenient rumor.

nodes.name: A Map in the Ledger
nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.dialogue: We copy every moon, station sentence, and circuit note into our shared ledger.{pause}Then we power down before the final prompt, leaving Koto's route and ours unwritten.{pause}The knowledge can travel even if this singular cartridge rests for a while.{pause}Above the bazaar, wet roofs hold the city upside down in their puddles.{pause}The little screen catches Mina's face, then Ren's, then only blue light.{pause}The bazaar keeps moving, but this one small mystery holds them still.

nodes.name: Good End: Circuit Archive
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: Above the bazaar, wet roofs hold the city upside down in their puddles.{pause}A tram bell crosses the rain and makes the whole stall feel briefly afloat.{pause}A rare cart can be expensive; a good story asks for a different kind of care.{pause}We preserve the save and publish only the clock circuit, credited to Koto's initials.{pause}Other builders can learn the trick without turning her private route into a trophy.{pause}Our completed shelf gains one empty stand labeled: a lighthouse still shining.

nodes.name: Good End: Yellow Umbrella Club
nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.dialogue: Above the bazaar, wet roofs hold the city upside down in their puddles.{pause}Their shared list softens at the folds from years of being opened together.{pause}Mina writes one clean line in the ledger before either of them moves on.{pause}We preserve the save and tell the vendor that Koto's planned handoff finally worked.{pause}He hangs her yellow umbrella above the stall, where pairs of friends now meet.{pause}The cart stays quiet, but its custom becomes louder every rainy market night.

nodes.name: Good End: The Open Moon
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: Above the bazaar, wet roofs hold the city upside down in their puddles.{pause}Even the silence feels playable, like a title screen waiting for one button.{pause}Ren checks the time, smiles, and decides the last tram can wait a little.{pause}We preserve the save and frame a copy of the marked tram map beside it.{pause}Visitors may follow the stations, but the last moon remains Koto's unopened door.{pause}Our shelf is complete only because it proudly keeps one question incomplete.

nodes.name: Good End: Second Circuit
nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.dialogue: Above the bazaar, wet roofs hold the city upside down in their puddles.{pause}Ren taps the case twice, their old signal for a find worth remembering.{pause}The tune returns to its opening phrase, now sounding almost like a promise.{pause}Our new route uses Koto's clock bridge and adds a dawn ferry stop of our own.{pause}We leave her save untouched beside it, two journeys sharing one blue shell.{pause}The shelf finally has a spine, and the spine has learned how to bend.

nodes.name: Good End: Passed Forward
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: Above the bazaar, wet roofs hold the city upside down in their puddles.{pause}The four-note market tune loops once, brighter on the last note than the first.{pause}Tonight the hunt is less about owning a thing than learning why it survived.{pause}Our first new stamp says: play with a friend, then lend one duplicate away.{pause}The vendor laughs when the blue cart returns to his stall for its next handoff.{pause}We began a route, but Koto's remembered rule decides where it travels.

nodes.name: Good End: Moon Route
nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.dialogue: Above the bazaar, wet roofs hold the city upside down in their puddles.{pause}Neither collector hurries; careful hands are part of the pleasure tonight.{pause}Every answer creates a smaller question, which is how good collecting works.{pause}We follow every pencil moon, then add one careful mark for the roof at dawn.{pause}Koto's map becomes a conversation across years instead of a sealed instruction.{pause}When the market opens, our two names glow beneath hers like small harbor lamps.

nodes.name: Good End: Builder's Ledger
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: Above the bazaar, wet roofs hold the city upside down in their puddles.{pause}Somewhere nearby, a vendor laughs and snaps another plastic case shut.{pause}They leave room for doubt instead of filling it with a convenient rumor.{pause}The copied circuit diagram starts a free workshop for handmade WonderSwan stories.{pause}Koto's save rests safely while new blue shells appear on soldering mats nearby.{pause}We did not finish her game; we helped its clever idea keep moving.

nodes.name: Good End: Biscuit Tin Library
nodes.speaker: Mina
nodes.dialogue: Above the bazaar, wet roofs hold the city upside down in their puddles.{pause}The little screen catches Mina's face, then Ren's, then only blue light.{pause}The bazaar keeps moving, but this one small mystery holds them still.{pause}The vendor donates Koto's biscuit tin, and we fill it with lending cards and notes.{pause}Every borrower adds one memory before passing a cart to another pair of hands.{pause}Our ledger becomes warmer than any perfect row of cases could be.

nodes.name: Good End: Little Atlas
nodes.speaker: Ren
nodes.dialogue: Above the bazaar, wet roofs hold the city upside down in their puddles.{pause}A tram bell crosses the rain and makes the whole stall feel briefly afloat.{pause}A rare cart can be expensive; a good story asks for a different kind of care.{pause}We print a tiny atlas of the tram moons and leave the final page blank.{pause}Collectors add their own safe routes, shops, friends, and rainy-night discoveries.{pause}The blue cart returns to the shelf, while its map learns a hundred new harbors.
